Software Version: ATL105 Specification Release Version: 2026-4 October 09, 2026 1-1 1. Introduction This document provides information about the BUYPASS® platform (BUYPASS) ATL105 message formats (software version ATL105). This format is generally used when a BUYPASS customer device accesses BUYPASS directly. The scope of the information contained in this document is described in the chapter descriptions listed below. The audiences of this document include decision makers evaluating BUYPASS services and the programmers and analysts who implement and support these services. Note: It is important to note that sending of Payment Application Data Security Standard (PA- DSS) sensitive information, for example PAN, in any field, other than those designated to contain such information, is strictly prohibited and can lead to adverse consequences. This document contains the following chapters and appendices: 1. Introduction. This chapter lists and describes each chapter in this document. 2. Message Flow Overview. This chapter describes the flow of messages from a BUYPASS customer device to BUYPASS. 3. Specifications Requirements. Software Version: ATL105 Specification Release Version: 2026-4 October 09, 2026 2-5 2.3.1 Time-out by Customer's Host/Controller/POS System This section describes the transaction flow for an unsuccessful financial transaction (request and response) resulting from a time-out by a customer’s host/controller/POS system. This transaction flow describes single threading (one transaction at a time); however, any combination of requests and responses can be in process at any given time. A time-out occurs at the customer’s host/controller/POS system when either of the following situations occurs: • The customer’s 30-second response interval expires without a response from BUYPASS. • A response from BUYPASS is received after the customer’s 30-second response interval expires. If the customer’s host/controller/POS system receives a late response to the original transaction request from BUYPASS, the late response is ignored. In the event the customer’s host/controller/POS system receives more than three consecutive time-outs in an IP environment, the line to BUYPASS is marked “down,” and a communications test/health message is sent every 30 seconds until a valid response is received from BUYPASS. Once a time-out occurs for a device, the customer’s host/controller/POS system formats a TOR, which is queued in the customer’s host/controller/POS system until the next financial transaction is initiated for that device. A TOR must be sent from the same device as the original financial transaction request that resulted in the TOR. When the next financial transaction is initiated from that device, the queued TOR is transmitted to BUYPASS ahead of the new financial transaction request. If a new financial transaction is not submitted between the occurrence of the TOR and the end-of-day settlement, the TOR should be sent to the host immediately prior to the settlement request. Some customer host/controller/POS systems allow transactions to be approved and processed in an off-line mode. When the host/controller/POS system detects that the line to BUYPASS is back “up,” the off-line transactions are forwarded to BUYPASS only after a valid response is received for all queued TOR’s. The Sequence Number, Account Number, and dollar amount—assigned by the customer’s host/controller/POS system—are the elements used to match a request with its respective response. The Sequence Number of a TOR must be the same as the Sequence Number of the financial transaction being reversed. Each time any financial transaction request is forwarded to BUYPASS, the financial transaction should be assigned a new Sequence Number by the customer’s host/controller/POS system. Any response from BUYPASS to a TOR, whether it is an approval or a decline, is considered a valid response and should clear the TOR from the customer’s host/controller/POS queue. The customer’s host/controller/POS system should continue to send the TOR—subject to health message rules—to BUYPASS until a valid response is received. If no valid response is received after three attempts on each available connection route, an error should be logged in the electronic journal, and the TOR should be cleared from the queue. BUYPASS declines a TOR request as an unmatched reversal when BUYPASS has not received the original financial transaction request related to the TOR; or when the original financial transaction has already been reversed. 2.3.4 Summary of TOR Processing Rules
Refer to the below list for a summary of TOR processing rules that are described in detail in the above sections:

• A TOR should never be attempted more than 3 times. • A TOR is considered complete with any response from the host, except a timeout or no response from the host. An approval and decline response are both considered to be a successful termination of the TOR and the TOR should be removed from the transaction queue. • A TOR can only be sent for financial transactions. To remove the hold on an authorization only transaction, the device must send a cancellation transaction instead of a TOR. • A TOR is not supported for a debit completion. • Multiple transactions, and multiple TORs, can be in-flight at any given time. The terminal or device is responsible for tracking the status and maintaining the queue of the outstanding transactions. • When attempting to submit a TOR for a completion transaction, the device must finalize the TOR processing prior to resubmitting the completion. If the completion is resent before the TOR processing has been completed, the device risks voiding the resubmitted completion. • A TOR must never be sent until the device’s 30-second timeout has expired. • In the event a device has multiple queued up TOR transactions, the device must throttle the submission of these transactions, submitting no more than one every 30 seconds. • A TOR should only be sent during the same business day as the original transaction.

Once this ID has been assigned, the vendor must send it to BUYPASS in the Variable Information (Element No. 113) of the Authorization Request. Also, please see valid entries in Appendix I. Variable Information Data Layouts, Table ID 18 (Card Acceptor Terminal Identifier Information) for additional information. Note: Due to higher instances of fraud, it is highly recommended that the off-line/forced authorization key on the software/terminals be coded with a flag that will disable the key. The flag should be defaulted to off, so that the software/terminal does not have off-line/forced authorization key capability. The flag should be coded so that key can be enabled/disabled through setup within the software terminal. It is also recommended that a standalone password be added to the off-line/forced authorization key, so that when the key is enabled, the owner/manager has the capability to allow only certain personnel to perform the key function. Software Version: ATL105 Specification Release Version: 2026-4 October 09, 2026 6-2 6.1 Requirements DUKPT PIN encryption (DUKPT) is the required PIN encryption method for BUYPASS processing. In addition, for effective key management, the following criteria must be met: • All personnel are excluded from handling keys in the clear except when performing an initial installation or when adding new or modifying existing customer store devices. • Personal identification numbers (PIN's) and cryptographic keys never appear in the clear. • PIN's and cryptographic keys are never retrievable by application programs. • For DUKPT PIN encryption, the customer devices and BUYPASS share the same derivation key (DKey).

Software Version: ATL105 Specification Release Version: 2026-4 October 09, 2026 6-3 6.2 Triple DES (3DES) DUKPT PIN Encryption Processing This section contains the following information about Triple DES (3DES) DUKPT PIN encryption processing: • Customer PIN encryption • BUYPASS PIN encryption 3DES DUKPT PIN encryption processing does not require the periodic exchange of PIN encryption keys as does master session PIN encryption processing. This is accomplished by storing a 3DES DUKPT key at BUYPASS and using the 3DES DUKPT key to encrypt a serial number at each PIN pad. One 3DES DUKPT key exists between BUYPASS and a customer. This means that potentially several hundred to several thousand PIN pads contain the same 3DES DUKPT key. A unique serial number is assigned to each PIN pad. The 3DES DUKPT key encrypts a PIN pad’s serial number; and the serial number and its encrypted form (seed key) are inserted in the assigned PIN pad. The seed key and its corresponding serial number can generate approximately one million unique PIN encryption keys. 6.2.1 Customer PIN Encryption Hardware security modules must be used to encrypt all PIN’s, following ANSI® PIN management standards. Transmission of a PIN among interface participants must use DES-encrypted ANSI® PIN blocks. The following data are required to encrypt a PIN block for transmission to BUYPASS: • Card’s PAN • Cardholder’s PIN • Generated KPE 6.2.1.1 Point-of-Entry PIN Encryption The following events occur to accomplish PIN encryption of a PIN block for transmission to the customer’s host system from the customer’s card reading device: 1. The PAN is read from the magnetic stripe card placed in the point-of-entry device by the cardholder. Other information may be formatted on the card and can be read by the system. 2. The point-of-entry device prompts the cardholder to enter his/her 4- to 12-digit PIN using a secure PIN pad. 3. The PIN is encrypted with the generated KPE. 4. The encrypted PIN block and the KSN are sent to the customer’s host system for forwarding to BUYPASS.

Software Version: ATL105 Specification Release Version: 2026-4 October 09, 2026 6-4 6.2.2 BUYPASS PIN Encryption The following events occur to accomplish PIN encryption of the encrypted PIN block received from the customer’s host system by BUYPASS: 1. The customer’s host system receives the encrypted PIN block and KSN from the point-of- entry device. 2. BUYPASS retrieves from its database the 3DES DUKPT key of the customer. This key is encrypted under the BUYPASS master file key contained in the BUYPASS HSM. 3. The encrypted PIN block, the PAN, the KSN, and the 3DES DUKPT key are passed to the BUYPASS HSM and translated into a new translated encrypted PIN block using the BUYPASS master key. 4. The encrypted PIN block is translated in the BUYPASS HSM to a new translated PIN block using the network’s interchange working key. 5. The encrypted PIN is transmitted to the network host system. 6. The pathway terminal configuration for the PIN pad value must be defined for 3DES DUKPT. 7. At the Bank FIID level the key representation for 3DES DUKPT must be defined.

Software Version: ATL105 Specification Release Version: 2026-4 October 09, 2026 6-5 6.3 DUKPT Derivation Key (DKey) DUKPT uses a derivation key (DKey) and a key sequence number (KSN) to generate a unique PIN encryption key for every transaction that takes place at a PIN pad. The DKey is comprised of two 16-hexadecimal (HEX) character halves. These halves are loaded onto the processor’s host and are associated with a given customer base. When concatenated, these halves form a key part. BUYPASS supports 2- and 3-part keys. 6.4 Key Sequence Number (KSN) Another ingredient in the DUKPT algorithm is the key sequence number (KSN), which is a 20- byte HEX field. The format is discussed below. During the initialization process, the DKey and an initial key sequence number (IKSN) are used to create the base PIN encryption key. Future PIN encryption keys for any PIN entry device are derived from the base PIN encryption key. The IKSN is 20 bytes but the right-most (low order) 4 bytes—the Transaction Counter—must be initialized to 0’s. Each PIN-based transaction causes the KSN to increment. The key is changed at the PIN pad each time the KSN increments. Because the same DKey is stored on the host and used in the injection of the PIN pad, the host is able to derive the PIN block in each transaction. The initial value of a 20-byte IKSN must follow the format below: PPPPXXXXXXXXXXEZ0000 Where: PPPP represents HEX characters (F’s); XXXXXXXXXX represents any 10-byte HEX character string; E represents any even HEX character (0, 2, C, E, etc.); Z represents zero; and 0000 represents the Transaction Counter value. Note: The Transaction Counter can be manually included as part of the IKSN or programmatically concatenated by vendor-supplied software such as MKIXOR.

Software Version: ATL105 Specification Release Version: 2026-4 October 09, 2026 6-6 6.5 Test Key A test key is used for certifications. The clear key components are given to the customer/vendor for PIN pad injection along with the KSN. Overall left and right halves are given. Contact your BUYPASS certification representative for additional test key information. 6.6 PIN Block Construction The encrypted PIN block is constructed from the combination of the entered PIN and PAN fields. Restaurant Credit card sales are terminal-capture and initiated as POS Authorization Only transactions. Transactions are stored in the terminal batch as pending transactions until they have (or have not) been adjusted for tips. Tip adjustments are completed offline at the terminal. When the batch is closed, the pending sales are marked to send and uploaded as POS Purchase/Capture transactions, including the approval number from the original transaction request. A Totals Request (999999 – Shift Read and Reset) follows the successful completion of a batch upload. If a communication error occurs during the batch upload, the terminal reconnects to the host and follows normal TOR logic for any sent transactions that have not received an ACK from the host. The terminal then sends only the remaining transactions in the batch and does not resend transactions that have already received an ACK. An exception report prints after a successful batch upload. It includes any transactions declined during the upload process. Restaurant Debit, EBT, and gift sales are host-capture and initiated as POS Purchase/Capture transactions. Transactions prompt for tips at the time of the sale. Tip adjustment is not allowed with these card types. At the completion of the business day, the terminal sends a Totals Request (222222 – Read and Cut Settlement) after sending the last batch.

Software Version: ATL105 Specification Release Version: 2026-4 October 09, 2026 9-13 9.3 Host Totals This section discusses the activities involved in requesting host totals from BUYPASS. The device must be able to support all requests for merchant shift totals and settlement totals. When requesting host totals, the device displays a prompt for entering a password and date. The password must match the data in the BUYPASS merchant profile that is obtained via a Table Load. The host totals are accessed by entering a 6-digit Totals Date code (Please see chapter 13, “Data Element Descriptions,” for a list of valid codes for Element No. 105, Totals Date.) BUYPASS maintains two sets of daily totals for each merchant: • Shift totals • Settlement totals 9.3.1 Merchant Shift Totals This section discusses the activities involved in requesting merchant shift totals from BUYPASS. Shift totals accumulate for each merchant from work shift to work shift. These totals are scratch totals and do not affect settlement. They can accumulate beyond a merchant’s cut time. These totals can be requested as read only or read and reset. Descriptions of both of these total requests follow, together with their respective 6-digit Totals Date codes. 9.3.1.1 Read Only Total Request To request shift totals as read only, enter the following 6-digit Totals Date code in the date field displayed on the device: 111111. Entering this code enables a merchant to view shift totals without resetting the BUYPASS shift total amounts to zero. BUYPASS returns the host shift totals for transactions done since the last shift cut [Read and Reset Total Request (Totals Date code: 999999)]. 9.3.1.2 Read and Reset Total Request To request shift totals as read and reset, enter the following 6-digit Totals Date code in the date field displayed on the device: 999999. Entering this code enables a merchant to view shift totals and reset the BUYPASS shift total amounts to zero. BUYPASS returns the host shift totals for transactions done since the last shift cut [Read and Reset Total Request (Totals Date code: 999999)], ends the current shift, and resets the merchant shift total amounts to zero. Use these totals to balance against the local totals stored in the merchant’s device. If the merchant fails to request shift totals at the end of a shift, the totals continue to accumulate at BUYPASS until a Read and Reset Total Request (Totals Date code: 999999) is made. The host maintains the shift totals and they are available until the first transaction in a new shift has been completed. This allows retrieval of the shift totals from the most recently completed shift.

Software Version: ATL105 Specification Release Version: 2026-4 October 09, 2026 9-14 9.3.2 Settlement Totals Settlement totals accumulate over a 24-hour period and are totaled once a day. The settlement time, also known as the cut time, is determined by the merchant. The merchant chooses a default settlement time and has the option of cutting totals before that time. A merchant exercising this option is referred to as a variable-cut merchant. Settlement totals can be requested as read only or read and cut. Descriptions of both of these total requests follow, together with their respective 6-digit Totals Date codes. Business day totals can be requested as read only for the current business day, the previous business day, or the business day before the previous business day. Descriptions of these total requests follow, together with their respective 6-digit Totals Date codes. 9.3.2.1 Read Only Settlement Totals Request To request settlement totals for a specific business day as read only, enter the desired 6-character settlement date in the date field displayed on the device in the following format: MMDDYY. Entering this specific date enables a merchant to view settlement totals for a specific date without resetting the BUYPASS settlement total amounts to zero. BUYPASS returns the host settlement totals for transactions that settle on the specified date. Using the Totals Date code of MMDDYY returns totals for transactions that settled on the specified date. Note: Settlement Date refers to the date when transactions actually settle. Unless the merchant chooses to end the business day at 2:00 p.m., settlement time does not coincide with the BUYPASS end-of-business day. In most cases, to retrieve totals for a current business day, request totals using a settlement date equivalent to the business day plus one day. Based on the merchant-selected end-of-business daytime, BUYPASS groups all transactions done in that 24-hour period and totals them; however, BUYPASS does not run a settlement until 2:00 p.m. Therefore, if the merchant’s end-of-day is 6:00 p.m., transactions for that day settle at 2:00 p.m. on the following day. 9.3.2.2 Read and Cut Settlement Totals Request This option can be used only by variable-cut merchants. To request totals for the current settlement date as read and cut, enter the following 6-digit Totals Date code in the date field displayed on the device: 222222. Entering this code enables a variable-cut merchant to close its business day before the predetermined cut time as designated on the BUYPASS merchant profile. If the variable-cut

Software Version: ATL105 Specification Release Version: 2026-4 October 09, 2026 9-15 merchant does not request read and cut totals, BUYPASS automatically closes the merchant's business day at the designated cut time. Transactions performed after close of business are included in the next business day's totals. Notes: In a controller-based automated fuel pump environment, the controller should be designed to connect to BUYPASS 30 minutes before the designated cut time and forward all queued trailer transactions to the host. This ensures that all authorization only/preauthorization transaction pairs are captured on the same business day. After all trailer transactions are transmitted to BUYPASS, the controller completes a read and cut total request (Totals Date code: 222222); however, if a read and cut total request is not made, BUYPASS automatically closes the merchant's business day at the designated cut time. If a device supports table loads from BUYPASS, receiving the Card Type (Element No. 14) value of “164” enables Auto Close in a device. 9.3.2.3 Current Business Day Read Only Total Request To request settlement totals for the current business day as read only, enter the following 6-digit Totals Date code in the date field displayed on the device: 333333. Entering this code enables a merchant to view up-to-date current business day totals. Note: Using this code produces the same result as following the instructions for using the Read Only Settlement Totals Request described in section 9.3.2.1, “Read Only Settlement Totals Request.” 9.3.2.4 Previous Business Day Read Only Total Request To request settlement totals for the previous business day as read only, enter the following 6-digit Totals Date code in the date field displayed on the device: 444444. Entering this code enables a merchant to view the previous business day’s totals. Note: It is possible for calendar days to elapse between business days. For example, if a Previous Business Day Read Only Total Request is made on a Monday, and there were no transactions done the preceding Saturday and Sunday, totals are returned for the previous Friday. 9.3.2.5 Business Day Before Previous Business Day Cut Total Request To request settlement totals for the business day before the previous business day (the third most recent business day), enter the following 6-digit Totals Date code in the date field displayed on the device: 555555. Entering this code enables a merchant to view the totals for the business day before the previous business day. Note: It is possible for calendar days to elapse between business days. For example, if a Business Day Before Previous Business Day Cut Total Request is made on a Monday, and there were no transactions done the preceding Saturday and Sunday, totals are returned for the previous Thursday.

10.1.2.1 Partial Approval Transaction A Partial Approval transaction enables a merchant to receive approval for the amount available on the presented credit card when the account balance is more or less than the amount of the Transaction Request. Credit networks supporting the Partial Approval transaction return an approval containing the following information: Note: This information is returned when a Partial Approval Indicator value of 1 is sent in Partial Approval Indicator (Element No. 121). • A Response Code (Element No. 83) value of F (Indicates “approval, partial amount approved.”) • Approved Amount (Element No. 6) contains the approved partial amount, and the POS device must prompt for payment of the remaining balance due on the sale. • The card balance—if returned by the issuer—is in the Additional Information Data Segment (Segment No. 112). Partial Approval transactions are supported for: • POS Purchase • POS Authorization Only • CAT Authorization Only The amount in a Reversal (Void) request must be the amount approved in the original transaction response when a transaction has been partially approved. BUYPASS supports reversal of a partially approved original authorization and NOT a partial reversal of an original transaction. The amount in a TOR request must be the amount requested in the original transaction response when a transaction has been partially approved. The Sequence Number must be the Sequence Number contained in the original transaction request.

Software Version: ATL105 Specification Release Version: 2026-4 October 09, 2026 10-7 10.1.3 Address Verification Service Address Verification Service (AVS) is a credit card authorization tool used for transactions performed primarily in a non-face-to-face environment, such as mail order, phone order, or customer-activated terminal (CAT). The device sends a transaction request to BUYPASS containing the AVS information in the Variable Information Data Segment (Please refer to sections 11.1, “Financial Transactions,” and 12.10, “Variable Information Data Segment,” for additional information.). The authorizer returns a response containing both the transaction authorization Response Code and the AVS information in the Additional Information Data Segment (Please refer to sections 11.1, “Financial Transactions,” and 12.11, “Additional Information Data Segment," for additional information.). BUYPASS processes all Purchase/Capture transactions when the Response Code is an approval, regardless of the AVS information. If the merchant decides not to accept the purchase due to the value of the AVS information, the merchant must perform a Purchase Reversal. 10.1.4 Bill Payment/Recurring and Installment Payment Transactions Support for bill payment/recurring and installment payment transactions is an optional service. These transactions must be identified by a Variable Information Indicator located in the Variable Information section of the Variable Information Data Segment (Segment No. 111). It is a contactless data transmission and capture technology. When applied to credit card processing, it refers to the capability of a point-of-sale device to capture and transmit full, unaltered Track 2 data from a card without requiring the card to have contact with the point-of-sale device. An RFID card has a chip embedded in the card that transmits Track 2 data wirelessly when the card is in close proximity to an RFID receiver. Most RFID cards also have a magnetic stripe on the back of the card that can be used with a card reader if an RFID receiver is not present. RFID processing requires that the appropriate values be sent in Point-of-Sale Entry Mode (Contained in Element No. 113, Variable Information.) on all transactions when an RFID receiver is connected to the point-of-sale device or controller. Even if the transaction is swiped, manually keyed, or uses a card type for which RFID is not applicable, Point-of-Sale Entry Mode must be populated correctly in the transaction request from the point-of-sale when an RFID receiver is present.

10.2 Debit Card Processing Requirements This section discusses the following debit card processing requirements: • Card requirements • Supported transaction types • Healthcare auto-substantiation service • Receipt requirements • Regulatory requirements 10.2.1 Card Requirements This section discusses the following card requirements for debit card processing: • Expiration date • Duplicate Completion transactions • PIN entry • Manual entry 10.2.1.1 Expiration Date The device does not perform expiration date validation on a debit card when the card is processed as a debit transaction. On-line authorization must be requested for the transaction regardless of the expiration date on the card. 10.2.1.2 Duplicate Completion Transactions When processing a Debit Card Completion transaction, the transaction can only be processed one time by BUYPASS and debit networks. This transaction cannot be reversed or processed again by the device. In the event the device sends a Debit Card Completion transaction to BUYPASS and does not receive a response, the device should resend the request on the next dial attempt or 30 minutes later—whichever occurs first. If the device receives a Response Code value of 1 (indicating a "decline") and a Decline Code value of 24 in the transaction response message, then the device should treat the response as already captured on BUYPASS and update the device totals as "approved." Any response from BUYPASS to a Debit Card Completion transaction should end attempts to retry a Debit Card Completion whether "approved" or "declined." 10.2.1.3 PIN Entry When processing a debit card transaction, the entry of the customer PIN is required on a DES- compliant entry device, and it must be encrypted using the DUKPT PIN encryption method. All transactions—except the Purchase Reversal transaction—require PIN entry. 10.2.1.4 Manual Entry Manual entry is not allowed on a debit card transaction. If the device is unable to read the card's magnetic strip, it should prompt the user to swipe the card again—up to three times. If unable to read the magnetic strip after three attempts, a message should be displayed to the clerk and the transaction ended.

In addition to those requirements, the following information must appear on EBT card receipts: • Tender Type and Transaction Type • Clerk ID • Voucher Number • Transaction amounts • Balances • Approved messages • Declined messages • Approved HIP transaction data No signature line is required when printing an EBT receipt. Optionally, a SIGNATURE NOT REQUIRED message can be printed. 10.5.4.1 Tender Type and Transaction Type The receipt must print whether the transaction is a Food Stamp transaction or a Cash Benefit transaction. It must also indicate the type of transaction attempted. Examples. Food Stamp Purchase Cash Benefit Purchase with Cash Back 10.5.4.2 Clerk ID Note: The Clerk ID is an optional receipt requirement. As an option, it may be retrieved from the transaction prompting sequence or a log on/log off function and printed on the receipt. Also, as an option, the device may prompt for a Clerk ID, whether it is on a transaction basis or within a log on/log off function. It/They must be broken down for purchases versus cash back and include a total for both—if both amounts were entered. 10.5.4.5 Balances For both Food Stamp transactions and Cash Benefit transactions, the ending balance must be printed on the receipt. As an option, the beginning EBT balance may be printed on the receipt by calculating the balance based on the ending balance and the amount of the transaction. EBT authorizers may return either a food stamp balance only, a cash benefit balance only, or both balances. If a particular balance is not returned, do not print a balance of zero; omit the

Balances of zero dollars should only be printed when zero is actually returned as the balance from the authorizer. 10.5.4.6 Approved Transactions The Approval Number and message from the transaction response must be printed on the receipts for all "approved" EBT transactions. The device may not prompt for reentry of the PIN without printing a receipt and retrying the transaction. 10.5.4.8 Approved HIP transaction data The following fields must be printed on the receipt for the EBT FOOD approved HIP transactions: EBT HIP Transactions: • Incentive Eligible Amount • Incentive Earned or Incentive Returned • Month to date Incentive Earned

Software Version: ATL105 Specification Release Version: 2026-4 October 09, 2026 10-45 10.7 Stored Value Card Processing Requirements This section discusses the following stored value card (SVC) processing requirements: • Process overview • Card requirements • Supported transaction types • Receipt Requirements • Postal Code Capture • Track Support Requirements 10.7.1 Process Overview A stored value card cannot be used for transactions until it has been activated. There are three activation methods: • Activation without using a device • Activation using a device (predefined monetary limit) • Activation using a device (customer-defined monetary limit; issuer-activated) Under the first method, a stored value card is activated before a customer purchases it. The card is ready to use immediately. This method requires receipt by the vendor of a fulfillment letter confirming the cards' shipment to the client. Under the second method, a customer purchases a sealed SVC package that has a predefined monetary limit displayed on the cover. The card is activated by swiping the package through the card reader of an indoor device. If the card's magnetic stripe is invalid, the entire package is discarded, and the process is repeated with a new package. If an "approved" Response is received, the card is active and ready to use—up to the predefined monetary limit. Under the third method, a customer purchases a stored value card that has no predefined value. The card is activated by swiping it through a card reader and entering the activation amount at an indoor device. If an “approved” Response is received, the card is active and ready to use—up to the defined monetary limit. The card can be used until its monetary limit is exhausted. Clients can determine whether purchases can be made under a specific amount (i.e. $1.00). If an activated card is not used within the time frame established by its authorizer, it can be deactivated at any of the participating client’s devices.

Software Version: ATL105 Specification Release Version: 2026-4 October 09, 2026 10-46 10.7.2 Card Requirements This section discusses the following card requirements for SVC processing: • Expiration date • Manual entry • Amount • Partial Approval • Embossing standards—First Data™ Premium Gift Card 10.7.2.1 Expiration Date The device does not perform expiration date validation in a stored value card transaction. 10.7.2.2 Manual Entry/Bar Code Manual entry may be allowed on a stored value card transaction. It is dependent on the authorizer. If the POS device is unable to read the card's magnetic stripe, it should prompt the user to swipe the card again—up to three times. When manual entry is allowed, and the POS device is unable to read the magnetic stripe after three attempts, the POS device should prompt for manual entry of the Account Number and Expiration Date (Manual entry format: MMYY). The value to be used as the expiration date appears as an embossed 4-digit number on the First Data™ Standard Gift Card and the Stored Value Systems card. An expiration date is not embossed on the front of the First Data™ Premium Gift Card; therefore, a default value of 1249 (Manual entry format: MMYY) is sent by the POS device. (Note: The First Data™ Premium Gift Card has a 16-digit Account Number.) When manual entry is not allowed, and the POS device is unable to read the magnetic stripe after three attempts, a message should be displayed to the clerk, and the transaction ended. If manual entry is used, this fact is indicated on the receipt and journal by an asterisk (*). Bar Code Scanned Gift card should be treated as a manually entered transaction. It should be send like a manual transaction with Account Number and Expiration Date in the designated fields. The entry mode should be “01”. Blackhawk Gift card transactions should be treated as swiped transactions. The entry mode should be received as “90” for Blackhawk Scanned transactions. 10.7.2.3 Amount When an activation (Please see section 10.7.3.6, “Activation Transaction.”) transaction, deactivation (Please see section 10.7.3.7, “Deactivation (Cash Out) Transaction.”) transaction, or a recharged/issued (Please see section 10.7.3.8, “Recharge/Issue Card Transaction.”) transaction is performed, a prompt for the activated/recharged/issued amount is required. 10.7.2.4 Partial Approval Stored value card issuers have the ability to approve a transaction request for an amount that is different from the request amount. When this occurs, the device will process the transaction for the approved amount returned in the transaction response and handle the remaining balance of the sale as a split tender transaction. When a transaction is partially approved by the issuer, transaction responses contain the following information: • A Response Code (Element No. 83) value of F (Indicates “approval, partial amount approved.”)

Software Version: ATL105 Specification Release Version: 2026-4 October 09, 2026 10-47 • Approved Amount (Element No. 6) contains the approved partial amount, and the POS device must prompt for payment of the remaining balance due on the sale. • Approval Number (Element No. 5) contains the card balance—if returned by the issuer.

When the transaction is processed as a split tender transaction the device will print a transaction receipt indicating the amount due on the transaction, display the amount due and offer options to complete the remaining balance of the sale. Other options for payment include credit, debit, EBT, cash, or cancellation of the transaction.

Software Version: ATL105 Specification Release Version: 2026-4 October 09, 2026 10-49 10.7.3 Supported Transaction Types The following point-of-sale transactions are supported for SVC processing: • Purchase/Capture • Purchase Reversal • Authorization Only • Authorization Only Reversal • Merchandise Return • Activation • Deactivation • Recharge/Issue Card • Balance Merge • Replace Card • Balance Inquiry • Cancellation • Cancellation (Time-out Reversal) The following customer-activated transactions are supported for SVC processing: • Purchase/Capture • Authorization Only • Authorization Only Reversal • Cancellation (Time-out Reversal) The following additional transaction types are supported for InComm: • Account Verification (Preauthorization Activation) 10.7.3.1 Purchase/Capture Transaction If an approved response is received, the card issuer deducts the purchase amount from the card's balance; otherwise, a declined response is sent to the device. 10.7.3.2 Purchase Reversal Transaction This transaction adds the transaction amount to the card's balance. This amount must be the exact amount of a previous SVC transaction. (The previous transaction must have been done in the same business day.) The POS device must subtract this amount from the SVC bucket and subtract this transaction from the SVC quantity. 10.7.3.3 Authorization Only Transaction This transaction places a lock on the card. The client decides the duration of the lock. The Authorization Only Response contains the card's balance and the authorization number. 10.7.3.4 Authorization Only Reversal Transaction This transaction is used if the device fails, or a communication problem occurs after the device receives an approved Authorization Only Response. This transaction has an amount previously set by the client. When this transaction is received, the card issuer unlocks the SVC account. 10.7.3.5 Merchandise Return Transaction This transaction adds the given amount to the card's balance. The POS device must subtract this amount from the SVC bucket and add this transaction to the SVC quantity.

Software Version: ATL105 Specification Release Version: 2026-4 October 09, 2026 10-50 10.7.3.6 Activation Transaction This transaction activates the SVC's Account Number for a specific dollar amount on the card issuer's system. After a successful Activation Transaction, charges can be made against this SVC account. 10.7.3.7 Deactivation (Cash Out) Transaction For non-First Data™ Standard Gift Card transactions, this transaction is called a Deactivation transaction. The deactivation amount in the transaction request must match the account balance. Depending upon the client’s configuration, after a successful Deactivation transaction, the stored value card’s Account Number can be closed on the card issuer’s system, and charges can no longer be made against this Account Number. For First Data™ Premium Gift Card transactions, this transaction is called a Cash Out transaction. The cash out amount in the transaction request must be greater than $0.00 and equal to or less than the account balance. After the request is received, the account’s balance is taken to $0.00, and the amount used to bring the balance to $0.00 is returned to the POS device in the transaction response’s Approved Amount field. Depending upon the client’s configuration, after a successful Cash Out transaction, the stored value card’s Account Number can remain open on the card issuer’s system with an account balance of $0.00. (Note: The First Data™ Premium Gift Card has a 16-digit Account Number.) The POS device must add this count to the SV1 count total. The POS device must subtract this amount from the SV1 amount total. 10.7.3.8 Recharge/Issue Card Transaction This transaction adds the amount entered at the device to the card's current balance. The added amount cannot cause the balance to be greater than the original value of the card. 10.7.3.9 Balance Merge Transaction This transaction enables a customer to combine the balances of two stored value cards in his/her possession, and place that merged balance on one of those cards. The account balance for the remaining card is reduced to $0.00. Note: The maximum number of cards that can be involved in this transaction is two. If a customer has more than two stored value cards in his/her possession for which balances need to be merged, the transaction can be repeated until all balances have been merged to a single card, and the remaining card balances are reduced to $0.00. 10.7.3.10 Replace Card Transaction This transaction enables a customer to transfer the balance of any lost, stolen, or damaged card to a new card with a completely new account number. Receipts may be used to obtain the account number for lost or stolen cards. This transaction replaces the lost, stolen, or damaged card. The balance on the account for the lost, stolen, or damaged card is reduced to $0.00. 10.7.3.11 Balance Inquiry Transaction This transaction is an information only transaction. It provides the SVC's remaining balance. This transaction should not change the SVC quantity or amount totals.

Software Version: ATL105 Specification Release Version: 2026-4 October 09, 2026 10-51 10.7.3.12 Cancellation Transaction This transaction is used to reverse any previous stored value gift card transaction. The transaction amount must be the same amount as the transaction that is being reversed. When this transaction is received, the card issuer unlocks the stored value card account. The POS device must subtract this count from the corresponding count total impacted by the original transaction. The POS device must subtract this amount from the corresponding amount total impacted by the original transaction. 10.7.3.13 Cancellation (Time-out Reversal) Transaction This transaction is used if the device fails, or a communication problem occurs during a transaction. The transaction has an amount previously set by the client. When this transaction is received, the card issuer unlocks the SVC account. 10.7.3.14 Account Verification (Preauthorization Activation) Transaction This transaction is used to verify that the POS, about to load/preload, is valid and ready to accept funds prior to accepting tender for the card. After performing the account verification, the POS may proceed with accepting tender and the activation. The subsequent activation is not associated with the original account verification. Note: This transaction type is only supported for InComm cards. 10.7.4 Receipt Requirements The credit card receipt requirements listed in section 10.1.7, "Receipt Requirements," also apply to stored value card receipts. In addition to those requirements, the recharge amount prints on all approved stored value card receipts. In addition to those requirements, the remaining balance (positive/negative) prints on all approved and declined stored value card receipts. The remaining balance (positive/negative) is returned as the Approval Number in the Authorization Response. No signature line is required when printing a stored value card receipt. Optionally, a SIGNATURE NOT REQUIRED message can be printed. In cases where the PAN is printed on transaction receipts, it must be truncated to its last four digits. A series of X’s equal to the number of truncated digits precedes these four digits for a field length equal to the original Account Number’s length. Truncation of the Account Number is required on all customer-activated transactions. The full Account Number should be retrievable from the POS device journal or transaction log for retrieval requests. Note: The last four digits of the 16-digit Account Number are truncated on First Data™ Premium Gift Card receipts only. In this case, these last four digits are replaced by a series of four X’s. In the case of either a Balance Merge transaction or a Replacement/Balance Transfer transaction, it is preferred that the receipt contain the Account Number for the card with the final balance. 10.7.5 Postal Code Capture Support has been added to allow a device to capture and send a customer’s ZIP Code™ in a closed loop prepaid card transaction.

(Please refer to chapter 13, “Data Element Descriptions,” for additional information about this data element.) The value of the ZIP Code™ is not validated by the issuer and does not have any bearing on the approval or decline of a transaction. The ZIP Code™ is used for reporting purposes only.

10.7.6 Track Support Requirements The following track support requirements must be met when processing all electronic stored value card transactions: • The default track that is sent to BUYPASS on an original transaction should be Track 2. • Card data provided in a Stored Value System (SVS) follow-on transaction can be either full or partial Track 2 Data. • Card data provided in a First Data™ Premium Gift Card (BIN 601056) follow-on transaction using either the token from the response or 601056* card number may be sent to BUYPASS as key entered transaction. • Card data provided in all other First Data™ Premium Gift Card follow-on transactions must be full Track 2 Data. Note: Partial Track 2 Data consists of the Primary Account Number, followed by “=” sign— rather than a field separator—followed by the 4-digit expiration date (Storage format: YYMM). No other discretionary data follows the 4-digit expiration date.

Software Version: ATL105 Specification Release Version: 2026-4 October 09, 2026 10-56 10.9 Loyalty Card Processing Requirements Loyalty card programs provide merchants with a system that allows consumers to accumulate real-time rewards, discounts, and messaging based on POS transactions. This section discusses the following loyalty card processing requirements: • Card requirements • Supported transaction types • Supported loyalty advice functions • Receipt requirements 10.9.1 Card Requirements This section discusses the following card requirements for loyalty card processing: • Expiration date • Manual entry 10.9.1.1 Expiration Date The device does not perform expiration date validation in a loyalty card transaction. 10.9.1.2 Manual Entry Manual entry is allowed on a loyalty card transaction. If the device is unable to read the card’s magnetic strip, it should prompt the user to swipe the card again—up to three times. If unable to read the magnetic strip after three attempts, the device should prompt for manual entry of the Account Number and Expiration Date (MMYY). The host returns the Loyalty Print Data in the response. The data returned to the device is a pre-programmed message maintained by the merchant at the loyalty host. • Points redemption This transaction is used to redeem points for payment from a POS device. Software Version: ATL105 Specification Release Version: 2026-4 October 09, 2026 10-59 10.10 Software Update Processing Requirements Note: Vendors who support their own applications do not use software update processing. Software update processing involves an automated request by an active device for a full application download to the device from the device management system supported by BUYPASS. The following steps must be included in this process: 1. A bit is set on the merchant profile at BUYPASS indicating that the device must request a DLL. 2. BUYPASS sends a Download Indicator of 1 in the response to the next transaction request from the device. 3. The device sends a Table Load request to BUYPASS. 4. BUYPASS responds to the Table Load request by sending the Software Dial Load Data Segment and Software IP Load Data Segment. 5. The device stores the data received in the Software Load response: a. New Software Version b. Software Terminal Record ID c. Software Load Phone Number or Software Load IP/URL Address d. Software Load Request Date e. Software Load Request Time 6. At the designated date and time, the device dials the Software Load Phone Number /Software Load IP/URL Address and initiates a request for a full application load. 7. Upon completion of the full application load, the device dials BUYPASS and requests a Table Load. 8. BUYPASS responds by sending the Table Load without requiring the bit to be set on the merchant profile. Notes: The device can attempt to request the automated full application load a maximum of three times. If a load request to Software Load Phone Number/Software Load IP/URL Address is unsuccessful, the device prints the “decline” message.

Software Version: ATL105 Specification Release Version: 2026-4 October 09, 2026 10-60 10.11 Electronic Mail Processing This chapter contains information about electronic mail processing involving a client, BUYPASS, and a client’s store point-of-sale (POS) device. 10.11.1 Electronic Mail Retrieval Data originating from a client can be sent to the client’s store POS device via BUYPASS. The data is sent to BUYPASS where it is stored until transmission to the client’s store POS device in one of the following ways: • A device operator, using the client’s store POS device, sends an Electronic Mail Request for the file to BUYPASS; or • BUYPASS responds to an automated Electronic Mail Request from the client’s store POS device. Either of these methods can be used prior to the end-of-business day, up to the time when a device ends its day. The Electronic Mail Request in either case uses a Prompt Code of 981. Note: For retrieval of proprietary card data, the Electronic Mail Request uses a Prompt Code of 996. There can be up to 750 bytes of print data for each Electronic Mail Request. 10.11.2 Electronic Mail Submission In addition, a client’s store POS device can send data to the client via BUYPASS in one of the following ways: • A device operator, using the client’s store POS device, sends data to BUYPASS using an Electronic Mail Request; or • The client’s store POS device sends data to BUYPASS using an automated Electronic Mail Request. The Electronic Mail Request uses a Prompt Code of 995. The Electronic Mail Request contains up to 217 bytes of data. BUYPASS sends an Electronic Mail Response to the client’s store POS device to confirm receipt of the Electronic Mail Request. The data is stored at BUYPASS.

Software Version: ATL105 Specification Release Version: 2026-4 October 09, 2026 10-62 10.13 Payment Tokenization Note: Please check with your First Data Certification Representative for the availability of this new feature. This chapter provides an overview and describes processing requirements for implementing the Payment Token processing feature involving the BUYPASS platform ATL105 message formats (software version ATL105). With the introduction of new payments, such as, mobile phones, and tablets, etc., the need for advanced protection against counterfeit, account misuse, and other forms of fraud, has increased. Visa, MasterCard, Discover, American Express, Interlink, Maestro STAR, NYCE, Pulse, Accel, and Shazam have introduced payment token which is the replacement of the Primary Account Number (PAN) with a token number that represents the PAN by device and/or e-commerce payment transactions. Payment token issuance is performed by a token vault that generates and stores the payment token and the associated cardholder PAN. The operator of the token vault is referred to as the token service provider. The token requestor is typically an acquirer, merchant or digital wallet provider that will use the payment token to replace the PAN in its database and in transaction processing. Payment processes that need to support token processing may include authorization, capture, clearing, and exception processing. Note: For additional information on payment tokenization terminologies, please refer to Appendix O (Payment Tokenization Terminologies) in this document.
Software Version: ATL105 Specification Release Version: 2026-4 October 09, 2026 10-63

10.13.1 Salient Features of Payment Tokenization Following are the general features of Tokenization: • Payment Token ranges will be in the existing ranges of the relevant card brand • Payment Tokenization is the replacement of the Primary Account Number (PAN) with a token number that represents the PAN by device and/or eCommerce payment transactions • Payment Tokens are mapped to the PAN, leveraging the existing payments infrastructure and messaging formats for authorization and processing • The Payment Token will be used for the entire life-cycle of the transaction for all card brands • EMVCo manages the Payment Token Standard

10.13.2 Payment Tokenization Usages A Payment token transaction, where the actual card primary account number is replaced by an association payment token, could take place in any of the following scenarios: • NFC transactions, when customer's NFC device is sending Payment Token instead of actual card number • eCommerce transactions with security data that contains token cryptogram, like VPAS, UCAF • Card-on-file transactions, where the initial transaction contains the token with valid cryptogram. The token and token related data could be saved by merchants, and used for subsequent transactions, like recurring payment The following sections describe the Payment Token transactions which are currently supported by BUYPASS: 10.13.2.1 Near Frequency Communication (NFC) - In Person Purchase Consumer has a device such as tablet, smartphone, etc. and the device has been provisioned with payment capability. A token is provisioned in the consumer’s device. The consumer walks to a store, for example, Coffee Is Us and buys a double espresso. He uses his “digital wallet” instead of the Coffee Is Us Merchant App on his smartphone/tablet to tap and pay. The tokenized card information is read and the appropriate contactless data is captured by the POS. Merchant submits the authorization as a contactless transaction exactly as they do today. 10.13.2.2 Mobile App (In App) – eCommerce Consumer has a device such as tablet, smartphone, etc. and the device has been provisioned with payment capability. A token is provisioned in the consumer’s device. Consumer activates the “digital wallet” on the device when using a Merchant App for purchasing. For example: the consumer downloads the “TV Store” app (an example of Merchant App) to his/her device. The consumer then decides to buy a TV and uses the TV Store app instead of going to TVStore.com website or to the physical store location to initiate the transaction. The TV Store App asks if the consumer wants to pay with the “digital wallet”. The Merchant App interacts with the wallet to get the token and merchant sends authorization request with appropriate data including the cryptogram.

Software Version: ATL105 Specification Release Version: 2026-4 October 09, 2026 10-64 10.13.2.3 Mobile App (In App) – eCommerce Subsequent Transactions (such as Recurring, etc) Consumer purchases 4 pairs of shoes on Fancyshoe.com via the Merchant App on their tablet/smartphone and decides to pay with the “digital wallet” on the tablet/smartphone. The merchant realizes that they have only 3 pairs in stock and 1 pair is on back order. Depending on the timeframe, the card brand allows the authorization to remain valid, while a new authorization may be required once the 4th pair of shoe is shipped. If a new authorization is required, there are specific field requirements that must be included in the authorization request for a token transaction to ensure that the subsequent authorization is not declined. Specific field requirements vary by card brand.

10.13.2.4 Card On File (COF) Consumer has established a relationship with an eCommerce merchant, where they select the option of storing their cardholder data (card number, expiration date) with the merchant for future transactions. In this scenario the payment token provided by the card brand replaces the PAN that is stored at the merchant’s end.

10.13.2.4.1 Stored Credentials A stored credential is information, including, but not limited to, an account number or a payment token. It is stored by a merchant, its agent, a payment facilitator or a staged digital wallet operator to process future transactions for a cardholder. A credential is not considered a stored credential when details of a card are stored to: • Complete a single transaction • Complete multiple authorizations related to the initial transaction, such as Incremental transactions Types of Stored Credential transactions are as follows: • Cardholder-Initiated Transaction (CIT) – A cardholder-initiated transaction is any transaction where the cardholder is actively participating in the transaction. This can be either at a terminal in-store or through a checkout experience online, or a subsequent stored credential transaction. • Merchant-Initiated Transaction (MIT) – A merchant-initiated transaction is a subsequent transaction with already stored credentials. The cardholder has given prior consent to the merchant to store payment credentials for future use without active engagement from the cardholder. Subsequent Transaction with respect to Stored Credentials: Once the card credentials are shared for stored credential at a merchant location or website, the following transactions are considered to be subsequent transactions: Standing instructions MITs: • Separate transaction to buy a different item, once again, using the same card at the same merchant location or website • Recurring transaction associated with the original transaction • Installment transaction associated with the original transaction

This section discusses the following EMV card processing requirements: • Process Overview • Card requirements • Supported transaction types • EMV PIN (Personal Identification Number) Processing

10.14.1 Process Overview EMV stands for Europay, MasterCard and Visa. It represents a global standard for inter- operation of integrated circuit cards (IC cards or "chip cards") through IC card capable point-of- sale (POS) terminals and automated teller machines (ATMs). EMV is used for authenticating credit and debit card transactions. The most widely known chip card implementations of EMV standard are: • VSDC - VISA • M/Chip - MasterCard • AEIPS - American Express • J Smart - JCB • D-PAS - Discover/Diners Club International There are two types of chip card technology – contact and contactless: • Contact - When a chip card is inserted into a card acceptance device, the contact allows the chip to connect to a reader. This connection enables the chip to get power from and exchange data with the terminal. • Contactless – When a contactless chip card is held within a couple of inches of a contactless-capable reader, the reader energizes the chip embedded in the card and allows exchange of data via radio frequency without the card ever leaving the cardholder’s possession. The benefits of EMV contact and contactless payment cards include: • Improved security against credit card fraud through use of a unique online cryptogram • Enhanced cardholder verification methods • Chip stores more information than magnetic stripe cards • Possibility for finer control of "offline" credit card transaction approvals In order to perform offline data authentication, a terminal must be configured with the necessary card scheme public keys. The card scheme (MasterCard, Visa, and Amex) Certification Authority distributes the card scheme Certificate of Authority (CA) Public Key to acquirers (i.e. First Data). Acquirers are responsible for the distribution of the card scheme CA Public Key to all terminals that support offline data authentication. Common AID is another application that incorporates the EMV standard. This application can exist on the issued card and the terminal that can be selected for performing a financial

Software Version: ATL105 Specification Release Version: 2026-4 October 09, 2026 10-81 transaction. There are four categories of Common AIDs. Any of these AIDs may be used in processing a Common AID transaction. • Visa Common AID • US Maestro AID • DNA Shared Debit AID • Discover Common AID The Common AID applications are actually implementations of VSDC (for Visa Common AID), M/Chip (for US Maestro AID) and D-PAS (for DNA Shared Debit AID and Discover Common AID).Those applications are licensed to other debit networks (like Star, NYCE, Pulse, etc.) and provide compliance with the Durbin amendment. DNA Shared Debit AID is used for ‘debit only’ cards that do not support MasterCard, Visa or Discover Signature Debit. Merchants should submit Visa and US Maestro Common AID transactions as ‘credit / 0100 / Dual message’ requests. This will provide merchants with optimal routing options. If First Data receives a credit transaction request with cashback with one of these Common AIDs, First Data will route this transaction, except Discover, to a ‘single message’ debit network. Discover already supports cashback on credit requests. First Data does not support cashback for Visa or MasterCard credit / Signature Debit transactions. DNA Shared Debit AID is limited to the ‘debit / 0200 / single message’ networks. As a result, merchants should submit DNA Shared Debit AID transactions as ‘debit/0200/single message’ requests. Cards supporting the DNA Shared Debit AID do not support Visa or MasterCard Signature Debit. If First Data receives a debit transaction request with cashback with this Common AID, First Data will route this transaction to a ‘single message’ debit network. Note: Please check with your First Data Certification Representative for the availability of this new feature.

If the account number is keyed, the device prompts for Expiration Date (Format: MMYY) and any other optional or conditional data, such as card present, AVS, or CVV code. Software Version: ATL105 Specification Release Version: 2026-4 October 09, 2026 10-83 MasterCard has mandated that Point-of-Sale devices that support EMV PIN must support both online PIN and offline PIN processing. Visa also supports this functionality but does not mandate online PIN support. This means that POS Devices processing transactions that are initiated from chip cards for credit and signature debit must have the capability to submit a PIN in the authorization request message submitted. Following are the two modes of PIN validation during EMV payment card processing: • Online PIN: This is applicable for credit or debit transactions, in which the PIN is electronically sent to and validated by the card issuer. The potential PIN requirement for credit transactions where a PIN pad is present is new with EMV. • Offline PIN: Instead of sending the PIN to the issuer, the PIN entered by the consumer is matched to that on an application housed on the EMV chip card. This functionality is exclusive to EMV card transactions. The authorization request may still be sent to the issuer. Note: In a traditional PIN Debit transaction, the PIN field is mandatory. Either a PIN or all F’s, for offline PIN, must be sent in this mandatory field or the transaction will decline as “invalid transaction”. In a credit/signature debit transaction, a PIN of all F’s is NOT required since PINs are an optional field for a credit/signature debit transaction.

10.14.4 EMV Fallback Transaction Processing For the purposes of this document, the term “Fallback” is defined as the acceptance of chip cards via magnetic-stripe processing at a chip-capable device. EMV POS Solutions must accept both chip and magnetic-stripe cards and thus have both chip and magnetic-stripe readers. If a chip card is presented at a chip capable terminal and a chip transaction cannot be performed, then the merchant may process the chip card as a magnetic stripe read (swipe). The resultant transaction is referred to as a fallback transaction and must be properly identified as such in the authorization message. Fallback transactions are less secure than EMV but continue to protect the merchant from the liability shift when performed correctly. Regardless, a Fallback will occur whenever an EMV Certified solution cannot read or obtain a viable matching AID. Software Version: ATL105 Specification Release Version: 2026-4 October 09, 2026 12-12 12.3 Product Code Data Segment This section describes Data Segment No. 102, Product Code Data Segment. Note: This segment can be used for all card types except for Comdata cards. Note: This segment is mutually exclusive with segment 157 Adjusted Product Code Data. Merchants should send one or the other but never both. If both the segments are sent, the transaction will be declined. When a Financial Transaction request includes the Product Code Data Segment, the products within this segment must meet the following requirements: • Fuel products must always be the first products in the segment. • For EV charging transactions, the EV fuel product code should be the first product code in the segment. • A maximum of ten products is allowed in the segment. • The total of product amounts in the segment must equal the total of the amounts [Element No. 41 (Fuel Purchase Amount), Element No. 58 (Nonfuel Amount), Element No. 99 (Tax Amount) and Element No. 17 (Cash Amount)] in the Standard Message Data Segment (Data Segment No. 100). • When tax product codes are included in the segment, the total dollar amount of tax products is also reported in Element No. 99 (Tax Amount) in the Standard Message Data Segment (Data Segment No. 100). • All fuel merchants must send fuel and nonfuel product data. Note: A unique Product Code must be sent for each type of fuel purchase. Note: With the growth of fleet industry and to fulfil the needs of the Over the Road Trucking (OTR) industry, BUYPASS can accept transactions with multiple fuels (e.g., purchase of Diesel, DEF, REEFER), all on 1 transaction. It is estimated that up to 30% of fuel transactions in OTR require fill-ups involving multiple Fuel Type Codes. Now, fuel merchants can allow multiple fuel fill-ups in 1 transaction. With the support of multiple fuels, a merchant must send the Product segment to BUYPASS with all the fuel codes and any non-fuel codes with all the relevant information like quality, unit of measure, unit price, and product amount. Also, the merchant must ensure to send the primary fuel (fuel used for the primary fuel need of the truck/vehicle) as the very first product code within the Product segment. Refer to the Product Code Data segment for the details on the product information layout and rules. This data segment can appear in any of the fields in Data Section No. 3. (Please refer to section 11.1, “Financial Transactions,” for additional information about Data Section No. 3.) It has a maximum length of 381 alphanumeric characters (001–381/a–z/A–Z). A Product Data Field Delimiter always follows Quantity and Unit Price. A Product Data Field Delimiter follows Product Amount when Product Amount is not the last element in the segment. 12.16.3 Proprietary Load Request Data, Prompt Code 903

A Prompt Code value of 903 is used for Site Configuration Data loads. This load type is used to send the site configuration data tables in a Proprietary Data Load request. In most cases, this will be a multiple message exchange between the Site System and the BUYPASS FEP. The Block Number starts at 1 and is incremented with each segment of site configuration data as it is sent. A value of 0 in the Block Number field indicates that all data was sent in the previous blocks. A value of 0 in the Block Number field is sent as a final message and does not contain any site configuration data on it. Site configuration data is sent to the host when a configuration change occurs at the site. If multiple configuration changes occur at a site during a business day, only the final site configuration data is sent to the host. If no configuration changes occur during a business day, then no data is sent from the site to the host. The Response Codes for the Site Configuration Data load are: • T – Approved—Proprietary load data, no more data pending • U – Declined—Proprietary load data, no more data pending

When a Financial Transaction request includes the Tax by Product Segment, the following rules should be followed: • A Product Code Data Segment (Data Segment No. 102) must be present in the transaction. • Each entry in the Product Code Data Segment (Data Segment No. 102) should have an entry in this segment too and the entries should be in the same order in both the segments. • Up to three taxes can be reported for a single product. If less than three taxes are to be used for a particular product, merchants can end the entry for that product early by using a field separator after the tax entry instead of a “\”. • If there is no tax associated with a particular product, the inclusive/exclusive flag should be set to “N”. In this case, the tax type and amount should be omitted. So, the entry for that product would only be the product number, followed by “N”, followed by field separator. • The only validation that will be done for this segment is whether the format is correct. No judgement will be made of the values contained. • For Canadian transactions, the valid values for Tax Type are GST (Goods and Services Tax), HST (Harmonized Sales Tax), and PST (Provincial State Tax). Any given product can have between 0 and 3 of these taxes specified in this segment.

Software Version: ATL105 Specification Release Version: 2026-4 October 09, 2026 12-107 12.41 Adjusted Product Code Data Segment This section describes Data Segment No. 157, Adjusted Product Code Data Segment. Note: This segment is used exclusively and allowed for Comdata cards only. Any transaction containing this segment that is not for a Comdata card will be declined. Note: This segment is mutually exclusive with segment 102 Product Code Data. Merchants should send one or the other but never both. If both the segments are sent, the transaction will be declined. Note: This segment does not allow any product codes above ‘899’ except for ‘955’ Cash Back. If any of these product codes is present, the transaction will be declined. When a Financial Transaction request includes the Adjusted Product Code Data Segment, the products within this segment must meet the following requirements: Fuel products must always be the first products in the segment. A maximum of ten products is allowed in the segment. The total of adjusted product amounts in the segment must equal the total of the amounts [Element No. 41 (Fuel Purchase Amount), Element No. 58 (Nonfuel Amount), Element No. 99 (Tax Amount), and Element No. 17 (Cash Amount)] in the Standard Message Data Segment (Data Segment No. 100). Since tax amounts are being added to the individual product amounts, there should not be separate tax product codes included in the segment. Instead, tax amount should be reported in Element No. 99 (Tax Amount) in the Standard Message Data Segment (Data Segment No. 100). Since Discount, Tax, and Coupon amounts are being accounted for in the individual product amounts, there should not be separate discount, tax, or coupon product codes included in the segment. All fuel merchants must send fuel and nonfuel product data if applicable. Note: A unique Product Code must be sent for each type of fuel purchased. Note: With the growth of fleet industry and to fulfil the needs of the Over the Road Trucking (OTR) industry, BUYPASS can accept transactions with multiple fuels (e.g., purchase of Diesel, DEF, REEFER), all in 1 transaction. It is estimated that up to 30% of fuel transactions in OTR require fill-ups involving multiple Fuel Type Codes. Now, fuel merchants can allow multiple fuel fill-ups in 1 transaction. With the support of multiple fuels, a merchant must send the Product segment to BUYPASS with all the fuel codes and any non-fuel codes with all the relevant information like quantity, unit of measure, unit price, and product amount. Also, the merchant must send the primary fuel (fuel used for the primary fuel need of the truck/vehicle) as the very first product code within the Adjusted Product Code Segment. This data segment can appear in any of the fields in Data Section No. 3. (Please refer to section 11.1, “Financial Transactions,” for additional information about Data Section No. 3.) Number: 11 Name: Block Number Character Type: N Maximum Length: 3 bytes

Representation: Fixed length of three digits Purpose: Identifies the specific proprietary or public key data block requested by a device or sent by the host. Processing Rules: The host always uses a Block Number to track the data block it sends in an Electronic Mail response and a CA Public Key File Load response. If response processing is interrupted, the host knows the Block Number for the last complete data block sent in the response. A device is not required to track the Block Number it receives in an Electronic Mail response. If it is required to do so, and processing between the host and device is interrupted, the device can reinstate transmission of the interrupted data block using that Block Number in the next Electronic Mail request it sends to the host. A device always uses a Block Number to track the data block it sends in a Proprietary Data Load request. If request processing is interrupted, the host knows the Block Number for the last complete data block sent in the request. A device is required to track the Block Number it receives in a CA Public Key File Load response. If CA Public Key File Load processing between the host and device is interrupted, the device reinstates transmission of the interrupted data block using that Block Number in the next request it sends to the host. Valid Codes/Values: Codes Description 000 The host sends the first data block for CA Public Key File Load. 000 The device sends this value indicating the last block of site / fuel volume data is being sent in the Proprietary Data Load request. 001 The host restarts data block processing, and sends the block that was Block No. 1 in the Electronic Mail response as the next block. <specific Block No.> The device can request a particular block by sending that Block Number in the next Electronic Mail request or CA Public Key File Load request.

Number: 121 Name: Partial Approval Indicator Character Type: N Maximum Length: 1 byte

Representation: Fixed length of 1 digit Purpose: Indicates whether or not a merchant supports credit/debit/fleet Partial Approvals. Processing Rules: Required on all transactions. Valid Codes/Values: Value Description 0 Not specified (default)/Not supported This value is the default value. If the Merchant does not support credit/debit/fleet Partial Approvals, then this value is transmitted. 1 Supported This value indicates that the Merchant supports credit/debit/fleet Partial Approval transactions. If the Merchant transmits this value with a transaction—and the corresponding network supports credit/debit/fleet Partial Approval transactions—the network can approve an amount that is less than the amount in the Authorization request; and BUYPASS will send a Partial Approval response. The network may return a card balance that is printed on the customer’s copy of the receipt. 5 This value indicates that the Merchant only supports the receipt of the card balance, not Partial Approval transaction processing. The network may return a card balance that is printed on the customer’s copy of the receipt. Note: This value is only supported for American Express prepaid cards. Note: Support for Partial Authorization is mandatory for all card brands. Data Element 121 ( Partial Approval Indicator) should be populated correctly for all card present transactions, showing that the terminal is capable of partial authorization responses. Note: For American Express transactions, Merchants sending transaction request amount as ‘zero’ and using values ‘1’ or ‘5’ for Prepaid card balances, will not be receiving the card balance back in response.

The exception record reflects both the approved and original prices for the transaction. The total transaction amount (Settlement Amount) is adjusted to reflect the total price adjustments, and is returned in the Approved Amount field.

Number: 190 Name: EMV Chip Data Character Type: ANSB Maximum Length: 999 bytes

Representation: Variable length of 999 characters, preceded by three digit length indicator All fields after the table length are in binary format. Purpose: Identifies the data sent in the EMV card to terminal interface. Processing Rules: Required in all EMV transactions. EMV data elements include a series of TLV (Tag/Length/Value) combinations which are required for processing EMV transactions. All data elements must contain the exact values that were present on the card to terminal interface. If the same data element appears several times on the card to terminal interface, this field must contain the last value that was present on the card to terminal interface during the transaction. Note: For the EMV transaction to be processed properly, the Application ID (AID) TLV (tag 9F06) or Dedicated File Name (tag 84) must be included in Data Element No. 190 (EMV Chip Data). Note: Tag ‘5A’ (PAN) and Tag ‘57’ (Track 2 equivalent data) must not be included in Data Element 190 — EMV Chip Data. Valid Codes/Values: The components of EMV data elements are described below: Component Name: Tag Each sub element or Tag can be either one or two bytes long. To determine the length, check the last five bits of the first byte, if they are all on (1) the tag of the sub element is two bytes long, including the current byte. Example 1: Tag x’9F10’ is a two byte tag - the last five bits of the first byte (x’9F’) are all ones. Example 2: Tag x’72’ is a one byte tag - the last five bits of the first byte (x’72’) are not all ones. Component Name: Length (ANSB …127) The next one or more bytes are the length indicator of the tag. To determine the number of length bytes used for this inspect the first byte of the length field. If the first bit of the first byte is a 1, the remaining bits (next seven) are a binary representation of the number of following bytes of the length field. If the first bit is 0, the remaining bits indicate the actual length of the data that follows. Example 1: If the length byte is x’0C’, then 12 is the length of the data that follows the sub element. Example 2: If the tag is x’82’, the length is contained in the next byte of the sub element. The value in the length byte indicates the number of bytes of data following.

Software Version: ATL105 Specification Release Version: 2026-4 October 09, 2026 13-139 Component Name: Value (ANSB …255) The data of each Tag/Length/Value combination is up to 255 bytes long, depending on the length of the field specified by the preceding length portion of the sub element. For an example of this data element, please see Appendix R. EMV Chip Data.
