Support, Testing, and Certification This chapter discusses the following topics: • Project management • Development support • General testing • Certification 14.1 Project Management BUYPASS uses a project management process. One of the main objectives of the process is to provide the best definition possible of the customer’s requirements. A customer project is submitted by a sponsor for approval. When a project has been approved, a project leader is assigned. The project sponsor identifies a customer representative who is included in meetings and receives project updates. The customer representative works with the project sponsor to construct the requirement document and identify critical benchmarks. The customer representative also works with the functional areas involved in the project itself. The actual management of the project takes place at BUYPASS. 14.2 Development Support Support is available for BUYPASS customers before, during, and after implementation of the interface between a customer’s device and BUYPASS.

Software Version: ATL105 Specification Release Version: 2026-4 October 09, 2026 14-2 14.3 General Testing BUYPASS provides a QA test system for the customer, vendor, or third-party processor to test new software code, modifications/enhancements to existing software code, communications, host interface functions, and other general testing prior to scheduling certification time. The client is assigned a test BUYPASS Merchant Number and access number to interface to the test system. Support by BUYPASS QA analysts is available. General testing includes the following areas: • Telecommunications  Connections  Line down • Message formats  Requests • Transaction types • Card types  Responses • Authorizer-generated for approved transactions • Authorizer-generated for denied transactions • Transactions denied by BUYPASS 14.4 Certification A customer, vendor, or third-party processor is required to submit a Request for Certification form once general testing is completed. This form can be obtained by contacting the BUYPASS QA department. It provides the BUYPASS QA department with the pertinent information needed to coordinate and schedule certification time. The certification process includes test plans and scripts, designed for the specific application requirements of the customer, vendor, or third-party processor. A BUYPASS QA analyst is assigned to the certification and provides support throughout the process. The scope of the certification may also require regression testing. Regression testing is a variation of certification testing.

Software Version: ATL105 Specification Release Version: 2026-4 October 09, 2026 Appendix A-1 Appendix A. TCP/IP Message Header TCP/IP is a streaming protocol, meaning that data received may consist of part of a message or parts of more than one message. Example. Message 1: “Hello, I am message one.” Message 2: “Message 2 is my name.” Message 3: “A third message I am.” Each time a receive is performed, one or more parts of these messages may be received: Example. Receive results 1: “Hello, I” Receive results 2: “ am message one.Mes” Receive results 3: “sage 2 is my name.A thi” Receive results 4: “rd message I am.” With no header or delimiter between each message, it is not possible to determine where one message ends and another begins. A simple delimiter such as a carriage return character would work well for messages that consist entirely of printable text: Example. Message 1: “Hello, I am message one.
” Message 2: “Message 2 is my name.
” Message 3: “A third message I am.
” BUYPASS has chosen the standard header method as described below. BUYPASS Header Field Name Size Description Message Length 2 bytes (16 bits) Length of the following data. High order byte is first (network or “big- endian order”). TPDU Protocol ID 1 byte 0x60 (Always use this value.) TPDU Destination Address 2 bytes (16 bits) Reserved for internal use. TPDU Source Address 2 bytes (16 bits) Reserved for internal use.

Software Version: ATL105 Specification Release Version: 2026-4 October 09, 2026 Appendix A-2 The message length includes the length of all subsequent data in the message including the TPDU area, but does not include the two bytes of the message length itself. The message length is binary data, represented in network (a.k.a. little-endian) order. Be aware that some processor architecture, such as the Intel® processors used on PC's store 16-bit integers in “little- endian” order, so the bytes should be reversed before sending or after receiving. Example. A 4660-byte message would have a length of 0x1234 in hexadecimal. The first byte in the header should contain 0x12 and the second byte should contain 0x34. Be aware that a 16-bit integer with a value of 4660 may be represented internally on your architecture as 0x3412, so moving this integer directly into or out of the message length field would not work. The sockets library on your system may have built-in library functions to convert to and from network order and the local host order on your machine. Note: The TCP/IP socket aborts without notification. Also be aware that the streaming nature of TCP may cause your application to receive the beginning of a message that contains only one byte of the length. The actual length of the next message will not be known until more data, containing the second byte of the length, is received. The TPDU area is reserved for internal use. Set all four bytes to 0x00 in messages to BUYPASS. Testing may be performed against BUYPASS certification system using the private BUYPASS IP network. Note: Check with BUYPASS Communications Support at the time of installation for the IP address to be used.

Appendix U. Visa Digital Wallet A Visa Digital Wallet can be of two categories: • Pass-through Digital Wallet • Staged Digital Wallet Pass-through Digital Wallet: A digital wallet in which the payment device/method loaded into the wallet is actually used to conduct the overall transaction but the wallet form factor (e.g., mobile device) substitutes the original form factor (e.g., plastic card). A Pass-through Digital Wallet provides functionality to a cardholder that facilitates the following: • Allows usage at multiple merchants. • Stores a credential (account or token) supplied by the cardholder to the Digital Wallet Operator. • Completes a transaction by transferring the stored credential to the merchant without interrupting the flow of funds. A pass-through Digital Wallet Operator (DWO) must ensure the cardholder consents in writing to the use of his or her account in the wallet according to the new rules, and must not perform Visa payment services for another DWO. Staged Digital Wallet: A Staged Digital Wallet couples two transactions, Purchase and Funding, each of which individually relies on and retains the character of the original, underlying legacy transaction methods. This wallet provides functionality to a cardholder that facilitates the following: • Allows usage at multiple retailers. • Uses a Visa account number supplied by the cardholder to the Staged Digital Wallet Operator (SDWO). • Uses a separate account or accounts assigned by the SDWO to the cardholder. • Completes a transaction (via an SDWO) in more than one stage, in any order, as follows:  Purchase Transaction: Pays the retailer using the account assigned by the SDWO.  Funding Transaction: Uses the Visa account number provided by the cardholder to fund or reimburse the Staged Digital Wallet.

Appendix Y. 3-D Secure Introduction: “3-D Secure” is a general term for an advanced authentication solution implemented to reduce eCommerce fraud by verifying a cardholder’s identity in real time. Each of the major card brands has a 3-D Secure offering: Visa “Verified by Visa”, MasterCard “SecureCode”, American Express “Safekey”. This appendix provides detailed information on these services.

How it Works: The 3-D Secure protocol operates in three domains: • Acquirer Domain – The Acquirer accepts eCommerce transaction data from the merchant and passes it to Visa/MasterCard/Amex/Discover (as applicable). • Issuer Domain – The Issuer is responsible for determining whether authentication is available for the card account presented in a purchase. • Interoperability Domain – Infrastructure created by the payment networks and software providers to enable the 3-D Secure protocol between the Acquirer Domain and the Issuer Domain

The 3-D Secure process involves the following steps: 1. The cardholder enters card information on the merchant’s site (that uses 3-D Secure) to purchase goods. 2. Merchant Plug-in (MPI) contacts the Directory Server (DS) to initiate an authentication request. 3. The DS routes the authentication request to the appropriate Issuer Access Control Server (ACS). 4. The DS sends the Issuer ACS response to the MPI. 5. The cardholder is directed to the Issuer’s 3-D Secure browser page. The Issuer authenticates cardholder’s identity in a variety of ways, such as asking to enter password which the cardholder has previously set up with the Issuer, or requesting to enter an authentication code/OTP that has been sent to the cardholder’s registered email/mobile number 6. The Issuer approves or declines the Authorization Request and returns the Authorization Response (containing cryptographic value along with ECI/Terminal Type (Position Nos. 9–10) values 25, 26, 27, 28 or 29 (as applicable) and other data) to the merchant. Refer to the below grid for the cryptographic values returned for each card brands: Card Brand Cryptographic Value Visa CAVV MasterCard AAV Amex AEVV 7. The cardholder is redirected to the merchant’s site and the purchase is completed.
Note: Contact your 3-D Secure representative for further details.

Appendix AA. TransArmor Processing Considerations
TransArmor is a processing option provided by FirstData that provides more secure transaction processing using encryption and tokenization.

When initializing a terminal for TransArmor Processing, a TransArmor Key Load should be performed to obtain the Key ID and Key to be used for encryption purposes. In addition, a RegiStart transaction should be performed to register the device with TransArmor. These functions are described in the ATL105 Specifications Update for TransArmor Processing document.
The available encryption types for TransArmor processing are: • RSA encryption • TA-VE Cipher Hidden Encryption • TDES/DUKPT • Ingenico On Guard FPE • AES DUKPT

The following are specific considerations required in transaction processing in order to use TransArmor. Data Element 2 – Account Number For TransArmor processing, the Account Number field is replaced by the TAP header and EDATA. The general format for this data is: TAPnnnnnnxyyyyyyyyyyyzzzz[EDATA] Where, TAP = 3-byte TransArmor Indicator nnnnnn = 6-byte Sequence Number of the transaction that matches the value in Element No. 86 (Sequence Number) x = 1-byte [EDATA] Identifier that describes the content of [EDATA] yyyyyyyyyyy = 11-byte Key ID zzzz = 4-byte Token Type ID. Valid Values: XXXX = Single use or MultiPay Token; 4-byte alphanumeric value assigned by First Data [EDATA] = contents are dependent on the information in the TAP header and whether the transaction is an initial transaction or a subsequent. Maximum length of encrypted data is 400 bytes. Note: On all subsequent transactions, the unencrypted expiration date should be sent in Data Element 12, Card Discretionary Block Data, as it would for non-TransArmor transactions. Note: In all cases, the TransArmor token to be used in the subsequent transaction is contained in the Account Number field in the initial transaction response. Appendix AD. Real Time Account Updater

Definition: The Real Time Account Updater enables the secure electronic exchange of account information updates between participating issuers and acquirers for merchants who securely store the Cardholder account information for future recurring / subsequent transactions (for example, credentials on file).

Transaction processing rules: The transaction must be from a participating acquirer and must be a card not present transaction as identified by any of the following criteria: • Credential on file transaction • Instalment payment • Recurring payment The merchant must register and certify with First Data to participate in the Real Time Account Updater process. Note: For further details and requirements, please contact your Account Representative. Participating merchant should send the Account Updater Request Indicator field (Variable Information segment 111, Table ID 060, Sub table ID 01) as trigger in request messages for all Instalment, Recurring, and Credential on File transactions. First Data will determine whether the transaction qualifies for Real Time Account Updater before requesting account information update from the association. Note: Merchants using Real Time Account Updater should refer to Account Number - Data Element 2 and Card Discretionary Block Data - Data Element 12 for additional information.

Appendix AE. Visa Estimated and Incremental Authorization Transactions

* MCC 4121, 5411 - Estimated and Incremental authorizations are allowed for Card Not Present transactions only. * MCC 5552 – Estimated and Incremental authorizations for EV transactions. For permitted merchants, an estimated or initial authorization must be included in an estimated or initial authorization request, and must be used when the final amount is unknown. In addition, merchants and acquirers must ensure that each incremental authorization requests: • Only follows an estimated / initial authorization. • Contains an incremental authorization indicator - BUYPASS Host identifies the incremental authorization transaction by the approval code returned (Authorization Identification Response). Once identified as incremental authorization transaction, the Host will send out the incremental indicator on behalf of the merchant to Visa. • Contains the same Sequence Number as the estimated or initial transaction request. • Contains the same Transaction Identifier in Segment as the estimated or initial transaction request. • Contains the same Terminal transaction number (Table ID 63 in Segment 111) as the estimated or initial transaction request.

Example: Customer A checks in a hotel for 3 days. The merchant uses Customer A’s credit or signature debit card (common AID - routed to Visa if processed as dual message) and sends the estimated auth indicator as ‘1’ in the Acquirer Trace Data – Sub Table ID 09 in the initial authorization request. At the end of Day 3, Customer A extends his stay at the same hotel and also avails a few other services, such as laundry service. The subsequent transactions must not carry the estimated authorization indicator in Sub Table ID 09. BUYPASS Host will identify the transactions as incremental based on the approval code that the merchant sends in Authorization Identification Response in the subsequent transactions. Merchants must send the final amount in the completion transaction message. For cruise lines, lodging merchants, and Car/ Vehicle Rental merchants, an approval response to the estimated authorization and any subsequent incremental authorization will expire 14 days after the initial estimated authorization. For other rental merchants, such as trailer parks and campgrounds, an approval response to the estimated authorization and any subsequent incremental authorization will expire seven days after the initial estimated authorization. Merchants with stays or rentals that exceed this period will be subject to chargebacks for no authorizations unless they complete the first transaction and then initiate the second transaction on or before day 14 or day seven, as applicable by MCCs.

Appendix AF. Estimated and Incremental Authorization Transactions

The Incremental Auth product is a means for a merchant to open an authorization, and modify it over time, before eventually submitting the final amount in the form of completion. This functionality has typically been used in the lodging and car rental industries, where the Initial Authorization may occur days before the transaction is completed, but is being expanded to support additional industries.

The Incremental Auth (IA) product supports four transaction types: • Original Auth (aka Estimated Auth) • Incremental Auth • Partial Reversal (aka IA Reversal) • Incremental Auth Completion (aka IA Completion)

This functionality is mandatory for Discover and is not limited by MCC. For Visa, Mastercard, and American Express, the use of this functionality is strongly recommended in addition to populating the Estimated and Incremental Authorization fields for the applicable lodging and EV transactions.

REQUIREMENTS: • All IA transaction types should contain Incremental Auth Data (Variable Information segment 111 Table 82). This is mandatory for Discover. o Incremental Auth Data contains the Transaction ID which must be unique (per terminal) to any open Incremental Auth purchase. • Incremental Auths, IA Reversals, and IA Completions are all subsequent transactions, and must be preceded by an Original Auth. • Subsequent IA transactions must contain the Approval Code (DE 39) that was received on the approved Original Auth. • Once an IA Completion is received, the IA is closed, and no more subsequent transactions will be approved for that Terminal Transaction ID.
